decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with an elbow-up lifting arc; right arm remains parked.
Advance toward the left tube while pitching the open gripper down, keeping the lifted elbow branch.
Align the left gripper with the tube axis and lower toward its body; final centering will use the wrist view.
Correct lateral wrist-view offset and slight approach tilt before closing; the tube is still on the table.
Fine-align the tube in the left fingers and close fully; retention will be checked during lift.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table while preserving the tube's grasp orientation.
Tube appears retained; begin a gradual upright rotation and transfer toward a left rack opening.
Complete the upright transfer above the rack, maintaining a closed grasp and clearance for visual alignment.
Lower the upright tube toward the left rack slot, retaining it while checking alignment near the opening.
Adjust forward over the left large opening and descend slowly toward seating depth.
Release at the rack and withdraw slightly to inspect whether the first tube has seated freely; contact may have shifted the grasp.
The first tube toppled onto the rack rather than seating. Lift clear and prepare to regrasp it from above.
Move above the fallen tube, gradually turning to a downward grasp without contacting the rack.
Finish orienting downward and approach the fallen tube from above; leave clearance to center it in the wrist view.
Replan with smaller pose increments after the continuity guard; continue the overhead recovery grasp.
Close around the centered tube at the current safe pose, then test a small lift away from the rack.
The tube moves with the fingers. Withdraw from the rack and rotate it upright, accounting for the lower recovery grasp.
Use half-sized withdrawal and rotation increments after the zero-step IK rejection.
Continue rotating the retained tube upright while retreating enough to preserve the elbow-up branch.
Make the recovered tube upright and shift toward the leftmost large opening, keeping it above the rack for alignment.
Bring the tube toward a large front-left slot and lower to inspect its tip against the opening before insertion.
Use the wrist view to center the tip over the large opening, descending only a short distance before checking contact.
The tip appears to pass into the opening without shifting in the fingers; continue a slow vertical insertion.
Contact suggests the tip may be at a rim. Lift clear and reposition over a more visible large opening before retrying.
Center the tip over the clearly visible large opening and begin a very short vertical insertion.
Make a millimeter-scale lateral correction and ease the retained tube farther into the large opening.
The tip is within the visible large opening. Release gradually and withdraw to let the tube settle and inspect seating.
The tube is not seated upright. Lift clear for a higher-body regrasp, avoiding finger interference with the rack.
Clear the left arm from the rack and begin an elbow-up right-arm approach to the outer right tube; the fallen tube remains for recovery.
Approach the outer right tube with a downward, axis-aligned gripper while returning the left arm toward home.
Finish the right-tube overhead alignment and bring the open fingers toward its upper body; park the left arm.
Shift the right grasp toward the cap so the fingers will hold the upper body rather than the tapered end; finish parking the left arm.
Translate along the tube toward its cap at fixed height, using the wrist view to obtain a higher grasp with insertion clearance.
Fine-align the right fingers below the cap and close on the upper cylindrical body.
Lift the right tube clear with a closed upper-body grasp before rotating it upright.
Transfer the retained right tube toward the rack while gradually rotating it upright at safe height.
Continue the upright transfer, keeping the tube well above the rack and the arms separated.
Finish upright alignment over a right-side rack opening, retaining the higher grasp for finger clearance.
Center the right tube over the rightmost large slot and approach the rim with the higher grasp retained.
Lower vertically toward the slot while keeping the tube held high on its body; check for rim contact before release.
Continue a slow, straight insertion; monitor whether the tube moves relative to the fingers or meets the rim.
The tube has stopped descending at rack depth. Open the right gripper and withdraw slightly to inspect whether it remains upright.
Withdraw the open right gripper clear of the rack and observe whether the released tube remains seated upright.
The released tube fell rather than seating. Clear the rack and approach the remaining tabletop tube with an axis-aligned overhead grasp.
Reduce the approach increments after the zero-step continuity rejection, preserving the current elbow-up branch.
Advance above the remaining tabletop tube with gradual rotation and clearance, keeping the left arm parked.
Finish the downward orientation above the tube, then use the wrist view for final upper-body centering.
Center the tube laterally and align its axis, approaching the cylindrical body just below the cap.
Center the upper body between the right fingers and finish lowering to the tabletop grasp height.
Fine-center the tabletop tube and close the right fingers on its upper body.
Lift the tube clear of the tabletop while maintaining its upper-body grasp.
Rotate the retained tube toward upright with a gradual, collision-free transfer toward the right rack openings.
Continue the smooth upright rotation and transfer, keeping the held tube above nearby objects.
